package_info.why_malicious: No specific software package or code is described in the report. The report discusses phishing TTPs involving brand impersonation in emails, such as embedding brand logos, using base64 encoding, fetching images from remote servers, and attaching images or PDFs. These are malicious at the campaign level, not as a software package.

execution_context.trigger: email delivery (phishing email received by victim)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the phishing email is opened, the HTML code displays a brand logo by embedding a base64-encoded image directly in the email, making the email appear legitimate and increasing the likelihood of user trust.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding brand logos using base64 encoding is a common tactic in phishing to bypass email security filters and make the email appear authentic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate brand communications typically use hosted images or official templates, not base64-encoded images embedded directly in the email body.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some marketing emails may use base64 images for tracking or design, but this is rare for major brands.
key_indicators: Brand logos not hosted on official domains

execution_context.trigger: email delivery (phishing email received by victim)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the phishing email is opened, the HTML code fetches a brand logo from a remote server controlled by the attacker, displaying it in the email to impersonate a trusted brand and potentially track the victim.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching images from attacker-controlled domains can be used for both brand impersonation and tracking email opens.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate brand emails host images on official, trusted domains, not unknown or suspicious third-party servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some marketing platforms use third-party image hosting, but reputable brands rarely do so for logos.
key_indicators: Image URLs pointing to non-brand domains
Use of HTTP (not HTTPS) for image delivery

execution_context.trigger: email delivery (phishing email received by victim)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the phishing email is opened, the attached image or PDF file contains a brand logo, making the email appear more legitimate and increasing the likelihood of the victim trusting the message.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Including brand logos as attachments is a tactic to bypass image-blocking protections and make phishing emails appear authentic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate brand communications rarely send logos as standalone attachments.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some onboarding or marketing emails may include branded PDFs, but this is uncommon for simple notifications.
key_indicators: Unsolicited image or PDF attachments with brand logos

execution_context.trigger: email delivery (phishing email received by victim)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the phishing email is opened, the HTML code inserts brand-related words (e.g., 'Microsoft SharePoint') into the email body to impersonate a trusted service and increase the likelihood of user engagement.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Inserting brand-related keywords is a social engineering tactic to deceive recipients.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate emails from brands use official templates and consistent branding, not arbitrary text insertions.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some newsletters or notifications may mention brand names, but not in a deceptive context.
key_indicators: Brand names used out of context

attack_chain.action: Phishing email is crafted with embedded or attached brand logos and brand-related keywords to impersonate a trusted company.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim opens the email, increasing trust and likelihood of interaction.

attack_chain.action: Victim is lured into clicking a malicious link, calling a phone number, or opening an attachment, potentially leading to credential theft or malware delivery.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive information or further compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Emails with base64-encoded images displaying brand logos
Emails fetching images from non-brand or suspicious domains
Emails with image or PDF attachments named after well-known brands
Emails containing brand-related keywords in unusual contexts
file_indicators: Attachments named logo.pdf, logo.png, or similar brand-related filenames
HTML emails with embedded base64 image data
network_indicators: Image fetch requests to domains not associated with the impersonated brand
HTTP (not HTTPS) image requests in email content
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor inbound emails for base64-encoded images in HTML, image fetches from non-brand domains, and attachments with brand-related filenames. Flag emails that use brand names in suspicious contexts or contain callback phone numbers. Correlate with known phishing indicators and block or quarantine suspicious messages.
